what: What dropping the honest-majority assumption costs, predicted before it was measured
the_question: This deployment is honest majority: Shamir, n=7, T=2, so privacy needs 5 of 7 honest. A dishonest-majority protocol (the SPDZ family) survives n-1 corruptions instead. What is the overhead?

what_actually_changes.sharing: Shamir over a polynomial becomes additive sharing plus a MAC share under a global key, so state roughly doubles.
what_actually_changes.online: SPDZ's online phase is two openings per multiplication. An opening in additive sharing means every party sends its share to every other, so 2*(n-1) elements per party. At n=7 that is 12; at n=2 it is 2.
what_actually_changes.offline: THIS IS WHERE IT GOES. With an honest majority, triples come from information-theoretic tricks --- random double sharings, hyper-invertible matrices, PRSS --- and cost field elements. Without one, every triple needs oblivious transfer (MASCOT) or somewhat homomorphic encryption (LowGear/HighGear). That is a qualitative change, not a constant.
what_actually_changes.robustness: Guaranteed output delivery becomes IMPOSSIBLE, not expensive. One corrupt party out of n can always stall. So switching would close off the thing ACCOUNTABILITY.md just showed is nearly free here.

predictions.quantity: online phase, MASCOT at n=7, elements per party per multiplication
predictions.arithmetic: two openings at (n-1)=6 recipients each is 12, plus amortized MAC checking
predictions.against: 8.000 measured for malicious Shamir online at n=7

predictions.quantity: THE HEADLINE. total including preprocessing, MASCOT at n=7, against malicious Shamir's 48.231
predictions.arithmetic: MASCOT builds each triple from pairwise correlated OT with a sacrifice, so a party pays roughly one OT-extension-sized transfer per partner per triple. Order 100 kbit per triple per pair at 128-bit security, six partners at n=7, is about 75 kB per party per triple against the 771 bytes measured for Shamir.

predictions.predicted: same order online, many more in preprocessing
far cheaper than MASCOT but still well above honest-majority Shamir, because triples still need OLE and cannot come from an honest majority

the_framing_that_matters_more_than_the_n.nobody_would_run_seven: The point of dishonest majority is that you no longer NEED many parties: one honest out of two suffices. So the real comparison is not 7-party Shamir against 7-party MASCOT; it is 7-party Shamir against 2-party MASCOT, which is roughly Prime Match's shape.
the_framing_that_matters_more_than_the_n.and_it_is_a_governance_trade: Seven KYB'd entities across regions is a consortium; two operators is a venue. DeFMI's whole structure --- regional in-region nodes, cross-region nodes, jurisdictional spread --- is built on the consortium.
the_framing_that_matters_more_than_the_n.what_dishonest_majority_actually_buys: Strictly stronger privacy and correctness per node: at n=7 it survives 6 colluding where the current design breaks at 3. It is not a weaker guarantee. It is a more expensive one that also forfeits robustness.

caveat: Both arms are MP-SPDZ implementations, and the honest-majority one was already measured at 6x the state of the art for its own regime (GSZ). A ratio between two implementations is not a ratio between two protocols.
